title: Prove without revealing
objective: Understand what a zero-knowledge proof is and how it separates verification from disclosure.
narrativeIntro: The Agency can no longer expose citizens to prove that a voter registry record meets a condition. You must learn to verify eligibility without revealing identity.

title: Circuits generate the proof
objective: Understand how Compact turns circuits into verifiable proofs and the roles of prover and verifier.
narrativeIntro: Understanding the idea is not enough. You must see how contract logic becomes a proof the system can verify to validate a registry record without learning its identity.

title: Explicit disclosure
objective: Learn when a private value needs `disclose()` before it can touch the ledger.
narrativeIntro: Privacy is not broken by accident; it is declared. You must decide which dossier data may be disclosed for verification and which data must remain protected.

title: Harden the mission
objective: Recognize the `potential witness-value disclosure` error and apply safe patterns.
narrativeIntro: When a potential leak appears, the compiler warns you. You must read the alert and fix the path before protected registry data is exposed.
